name: Seedspitter
body:
Seedspitter
CR 2

A cyan tube, as tall as a man, springs from the ground, culminating with a great, pink flower in the center of which a red vase-like tube slowly opens at your approach.

XP 600
N Medium plant
Init +3; Senses blindsight 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +0

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 13, flat-footed 15 (+3 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 19 (3d8+6)
Fort +5; Ref +4; Will +1
DR 5/slashing; Immune plant traits; Resist fire 10
Weaknesses vulnerable to cold

OFFENSE

Speed 5 ft.
Melee slam +4 (1d4+3)
Ranged seed spit +5 (1d6+2 plus poison)

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 16, Con 14, Int —, Wis 10, Cha 9
Base Atk +2; CMB +4; CMD 17

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Poison (Ex)

Seed spit—injury; save Fort DC 13; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d2 Con damage; cure 1 save.

Seed Spit (Ex)

A seedspitter can spit out a seed at high velocity as a ranged attack with a range increment of 20 ft. and a maximum range of 100 feet, dealing bludgeoning and piercing damage.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate or warm forests or plains
Organization solitary, group (2-5), or grove (6-18)
Treasure incidental

Seedspitters were reportedly created by a mad wizard or druid as a security measure for his lair. Unlike many dangerous plant creatures, they do not depend on their prey to sustain themselves. They do, however, hunt to reproduce. Seedspitters are tall and quite pretty flowers, mostly pink but sometimes red or yellow. Their large gynoecium, while similar in color, looks more like a pitcher plant than a part of the flower. It is where seeds of this plant are stored, dozens at a time, ready to launch at incredible speeds by their muscle-like container. The seeds themselves carry little nutrients, but have a very hard shell with a curve suited to both flight and puncturing targets. The pitcher is filled with a fluid toxin that coats the seeds, making wounds caused by them more lethal.

The seedspitters don’t discriminate, attacking any creature of at least small size that comes into the range of their senses. A creature killed by the seedspitter then functions as a nutrient-rich environment for the seeds lodged inside the wounds and they grow rapidly, making use of those conditions. While seedspitters are technically mobile, they don’t uproot themselves unless they have to, which is most often either when their surroundings become inhospitable or the soil dries up. Similarly, while their strong, rubbery stalk can work as a bludgeoning weapon, they never enter melee when they could instead spit a seed at the target. Seedspitters are rarely solitary, growing in clusters as large as possible given the circumstances and it is not uncommon for a whole grove of those murderous plants to develop when they are not pruned by well-equipped humanoids or a beast large and tough enough to trample the whole lot in rage. Some say that seedspitters develop a collective intelligence to rival that of animals when enough of them gathers, but so far there has been little evidence to support that theory, except perhaps curiously synchronized ambushes that groups of those plants sometimes spring.

Seedspitters can tolerate hot environments extremely well, as long as they are somewhat humid. They are leathery, tough plants and are hard to destroy with tools suboptimal for the job, sharp cutting weapons being the preferable option.

Seedspitters quickly stiffen and die off in the cold, and freezing them with magic is a safe and practical way of removing those plants for those who can muster such methods.

While their poison isn’t extremely potent, it can be lethal even to humans, especially those already softened by the devastating impact of the seed that bore it. As seedspitters pour all of their own excess energy into stockpiling seeds, most victims are shot at multiple times and sometimes even once or twice after already ceasing movement and succumbing to the wounds. While the poison itself most often spills out of the pitcher when the plant is killed with violence and loses all potency when frozen, there are always the brave, insane and desperate for coin that try to recover and sell the toxin, which is itself quite easy to alchemically stabilize and can be a valid source of coin on the black market, provided one has a way to both gather it safely, carefully and undertakes the necessary procedures within an hour of “beheading” the plant. There are rumors of shady groups, assassins and gangs that cultivate seedspitters for this very reason, but given the plant’s size, danger and the difficulty of the potential harvest, those are mostly unfounded.
